abbeyleix-heritage-house.expected_en: A heritage centre telling the story of planned Georgian Abbeyleix and of the local carpet industry.

achill-island.expected_en: Ireland's largest island, linked by a bridge, with the Croaghaun cliffs, wild beaches and the village of Keel.

acres-lake-floating-boardwalk.expected_en: A 600 m floating boardwalk over Lough Allen, part of the Shannon Blueway, with trails and kayaking.

adare-village.expected_en: A village considered Ireland's prettiest, with thatched cottages, monasteries and the Desmond castle.

aillwee-caves.expected_en: A cave system in the Burren with stone formations and an underground waterfall.

altamont-gardens.expected_en: Romantic 18th-century gardens with a lake, arboretum and the "azalea walk" — free entry.

annes-grove-gardens.expected_en: A former Annesley family estate in north Cork, with Robinsonian-style landscaped gardens and a rare collection of flowering shrubs.

aran-islands.expected_en: Gaelic islands at the mouth of Galway Bay, famous for their stone forts and traditional culture.

aras-an-uachtarain.expected_en: The official residence of the President of Ireland, in Phoenix Park, with free guided tours on Saturdays, subject to State business.

arbour-hill-cemetery.expected_en: A military cemetery where 14 of the executed leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising are buried.

ardagh-heritage-village.expected_en: An award-winning heritage village, with a picturesque village green and an interpretive centre.

ardfert-cathedral.expected_en: A group of three medieval churches, the oldest from the 12th century, on the site of the monastery founded by St Brendan the Navigator.

ardmore-round-tower.expected_en: St Declan's monastic site with a 30 m round tower, a carved cathedral and an early oratory.

ards-forest-park.expected_en: A forested peninsula with beaches, Franciscan ruins and coastal trails facing Sheephaven Bay.

arigna-mining-experience.expected_en: A guided tour of a real coal mine led by former miners, in the Arigna hills.

askeaton-castle.expected_en: Ruins of a medieval fortress of 1199 in the centre of Askeaton, former base of the Earls of Desmond — currently closed, exterior viewing only.

athenry-castle.expected_en: A 13th-century tower house that guarded a strategic ford on the River Clareen, in the centre of one of Ireland's best-preserved medieval towns.

avondale-forest-park.expected_en: A forest park with trails, treetop walks and history linked to Charles Stewart Parnell.

ballyhack-castle.expected_en: A tower house of around 1450 above the Waterford estuary, probably built by the Knights Hospitallers of St John.

banna-strand.expected_en: A long beach of golden sand north of Tralee, with dunes and waters ideal for surfing and swimming.

barryscourt-castle.expected_en: One of the finest examples of an Irish tower house, built between 1392 and 1420, with restored halls and a herb garden.

battle-of-the-boyne-visitor-centre.expected_en: A visitor centre telling the story of the 1690 Battle of the Boyne, at Oldbridge House.

bective-abbey.expected_en: Ruins of a 12th-century Cistercian abbey on the banks of the River Boyne, a filming location for Braveheart.

belturbet-railway-station.expected_en: A restored narrow-gauge railway station, with a railway museum and period carriages.

belvedere-house-gardens.expected_en: An 18th-century country house with gardens, the "Jealous Wall" folly and family events all year round.

benbulben.expected_en: A limestone table mountain and symbol of Sligo, immortalised by Yeats, with a ridge trail and an easy walk at its base.

birr-castle-demesne.expected_en: The Parsons' scientific estate with award-winning gardens, the giant 19th-century telescope and a science centre.

blackrock-castle-observatory.expected_en: A 16th-century castle turned astronomical science observatory on the banks of the River Lee.

blarney-castle.expected_en: A medieval castle famous for the Blarney Stone, whose kiss grants "the gift of eloquence".

blasket-centre-ionad-an-bhlascaoid.expected_en: A heritage centre dedicated to the Irish-speaking community of the Blasket Islands, with interactive exhibitions and a viewpoint over the Atlantic.

borris-house.expected_en: The ancestral home of the MacMurrough Kavanaghs, kings of Leinster, with Tudor halls and a craft market.

boyle-abbey.expected_en: A 12th-century Cistercian abbey with an impressive cloister, in the heart of Boyle.

bray-head.expected_en: A coastal trail with a large cross at the summit and views of Bray Bay and the Wicklow Mountains.

brigits-garden.expected_en: Gardens inspired by the Celtic festivals, with a sun garden, ancient woodland and a natural playground.

brittas-bay-beach.expected_en: One of the east coast's finest beaches, with 4 km of golden sand and protected dunes.

brownshill-dolmen.expected_en: A dolmen with the largest capstone in Europe: 100 tonnes of granite resting on 5,000-year-old support stones.

bunratty-castle-folk-park.expected_en: A restored 15th-century castle with a folk park recreating rural Irish life.

burren-national-park.expected_en: A unique limestone karst landscape with rare flora and trails in County Clare.

cahir-castle.expected_en: One of Ireland's best-preserved castles, from the 13th century, on an island in the River Suir.

carlingford.expected_en: A preserved medieval village on the shores of Carlingford Lough, with town walls, a castle and the Carlingford Oyster Festival.

castle-leslie-estate.expected_en: A Leslie family estate since 1660, with a Victorian castle, an equestrian centre, a lake and trails.

castlecomer-discovery-park.expected_en: An adventure park in 80 acres of woodland, with treetop walks, zip lines, canoeing and trails.

cavan-burren-park.expected_en: A karst landscape with megaliths, dolmens and interpretive trails in the Marble Arch Caves Global Geopark.

cavan-county-museum.expected_en: An award-winning museum with Ireland's largest outdoor First World War trench replica.

ceide-fields.expected_en: A 5,500-year-old Neolithic field system, the most extensive in the world, beneath the blanket bog of north Mayo.

charles-fort.expected_en: A 17th-century star fort at the entrance to Kinsale harbour.

charleville-forest-castle.expected_en: A 19th-century neo-Gothic castle surrounded by ancient oak woodland, with tours and events.

clonmacnoise.expected_en: One of medieval Europe's most important monasteries, on the banks of the River Shannon, with round towers and high crosses.

cobh.expected_en: A historic port town, the Titanic's last port of call and the departure point of millions of emigrants.

connemara-national-park.expected_en: A national park of mountains, bogs and wild ponies, with trails up Diamond Hill.

coole-park.expected_en: A nature reserve and former Lady Gregory estate, heart of the Irish Literary Revival.

cork-city-gaol.expected_en: A former Victorian prison with wax figures and an audio guide covering two centuries of prison life.

croagh-patrick.expected_en: St Patrick's holy mountain (764 m), with an annual pilgrimage and views over Clew Bay and its 365 islands.

curracloe-beach.expected_en: An 11 km stretch of fine sandy beach, location of the opening of "Saving Private Ryan", with dunes and trails.

donegal-castle.expected_en: A restored O'Donnell fortress with an adjoining Jacobean mansion, in the centre of Donegal Town.

doneraile-park.expected_en: An 18th-century landscaped park with deer, trails and a playground — free entry.

doolin-cave.expected_en: A cave with one of the largest free-hanging stalactites in the world.

downpatrick-head.expected_en: A headland with the Dún Briste sea stack ("broken track"), an old church and St Patrick's well above the Atlantic.

dowth.expected_en: The third great passage tomb of Brú na Bóinne, 5,000 years old, open to guided visits.

drumcliffe.expected_en: A 6th-century monastic site with a high cross and round tower, where W.B. Yeats is buried.

dublin-zoo.expected_en: A zoo in Phoenix Park with animals from around the world and conservation programmes.

ducketts-grove.expected_en: Victorian Gothic ruins of the Duckett mansion, with restored walled gardens and a public park.

dun-a-ri-forest-park.expected_en: A forest park with ice houses, a Roman bridge and local legends, on the banks of the River Cabra.

dun-laoghaire-east-pier.expected_en: A 1.3 km seafront promenade with views of Dublin Bay, ideal for a walk by the sea.

dunmore-cave.expected_en: A limestone cave with dramatic formations and a history linked to a 10th-century Viking attack.

dursey-island.expected_en: An inhabited island at the end of the Beara Peninsula, reached by Ireland's only cable car, with coastal trails and seabird colonies.

emo-court.expected_en: An 18th-century neoclassical mansion with gardens and a lake designed by Capability Brown; free entry.

glendeer-pet-farm.expected_en: An animal farm open to visitors, with goats, lambs, birds and an indoor playground.

government-buildings.expected_en: The seat of Irish government departments and the last major public building constructed by the British in Ireland, with free guided tours on Saturdays.

granard-motte-bailey.expected_en: A 12th-century Norman motte on an ancient hill, with a St Kitirine statue and wide views.

great-sugar-loaf.expected_en: A dome-shaped mountain peak with panoramic views of the Wicklow Mountains and the coast.

jameson-distillery-midleton.expected_en: A historic distillery where Jameson whiskey is produced, with guided tours and tastings.

kells-historic-town.expected_en: A historic monastic town, former home of the Book of Kells, with high crosses and a round tower.

kerry-cliffs.expected_en: Cliffs over 300 metres high with views of Skellig Michael, on the Skellig Ring.

kilbeggan-distillery.expected_en: The world's oldest licensed distillery (1757), with a working steam mill and tastings.

kilkee-cliffs.expected_en: A coastal walkway along cliffs with distinctive rock formations.

killykeen-forest-park.expected_en: Wooded peninsulas among the islands of Lough Oughter, with trails, kayaking and fishing.

king-johns-castle-carlingford.expected_en: A 12th-century Norman fortress above Carlingford Lough, with a medieval hall and views of the Mourne Mountains.

kinsale.expected_en: A picturesque coastal town with colourful streets, award-winning food and a rich maritime history.

knowth.expected_en: A great Neolithic passage tomb with the largest collection of megalithic art in western Europe.

kylemore-abbey.expected_en: A 19th-century abbey and castle in a stunning lakeside setting in Connemara.

lahinch-beach.expected_en: A sandy beach popular for surfing and sea swimming on Ireland's west coast.

lough-rynn-castle-gardens.expected_en: Historic gardens of the Clements estate, with a maze, a walled garden and views over the lake.

ormond-castle.expected_en: Ireland's only Elizabethan manor house, built by Thomas Butler, 10th Earl of Ormond, alongside medieval towers.

parkes-castle.expected_en: A restored 17th-century fortified castle on the shores of Lough Gill, with an exhibition about the plantation.

patrick-kavanagh-centre.expected_en: A centre dedicated to the poet Patrick Kavanagh in the old church of Inniskeen, his birthplace.

pearse-museum-st-endas-park.expected_en: A museum in the house where Patrick Pearse lived and ran his Irish-speaking school between 1910 and 1916, set in a park of about 20 hectares.

phoenix-park.expected_en: One of Europe's largest enclosed city parks, home to wild deer, the presidential residence and Dublin Zoo.

phoenix-park-peoples-flower-gardens.expected_en: A 9-hectare Victorian flower garden inside Phoenix Park, with an ornamental lake, playground and seasonal flower beds.

phoenix-park-visitor-centre-ashtown-cast.expected_en: The Phoenix Park visitor centre beside Ashtown Castle, a rediscovered tower house, with a Victorian walled garden and exhibitions.

pollardstown-fen.expected_en: Ireland's largest fen (alkaline marsh), a nature reserve with boardwalks and rare plants of glacial origin.

portmarnock-beach.expected_en: A long sandy beach north of Dublin, popular for walks, swimming and water sports.

portumna-castle-gardens.expected_en: A 17th-century fortified mansion on the shores of Lough Derg, with restored gardens and a forest park.

powerscourt-estate.expected_en: A historic mansion with award-winning gardens and the Waterfall Terrace; there is also a shopping centre and café.

powerscourt-waterfall.expected_en: Ireland's highest waterfall, at 121 metres, surrounded by forest trails.

proleek-dolmen.expected_en: A megalithic dolmen with a 40-tonne capstone, wrapped in legend — whoever lands a stone on top will have good luck.

queen-maeves-trail-knocknarea.expected_en: A trail up to Queen Medb's cairn of stones on the summit of Knocknarea, with views of Sligo and the Atlantic.

rathcroghan.expected_en: The ancient royal capital of Connacht and gateway to the Otherworld in Irish mythology.

rathfarnham-castle.expected_en: A 16th-century Elizabethan castle with four towers, remodelled in the 18th century, with family portraits and cultural exhibitions.

reginals-tower.expected_en: A 13th-century Viking tower, Ireland's oldest civic building in continuous use.

ring-of-kerry.expected_en: A 179 km scenic circular route around the Iveragh Peninsula, with spectacular coastal views.

rock-of-cashel.expected_en: A spectacular medieval complex on a limestone outcrop: Gothic cathedral, Romanesque chapel and round tower.

rock-of-dunamase.expected_en: A ruined Norman fortress on a rocky outcrop, with 360° views across the Laois countryside.

roscommon-castle.expected_en: A 13th-century Norman castle in evocative ruins, surrounded by a public park and lake.

roscrea-heritage-centre-roscrea-castle-a.expected_en: A group of buildings in the centre of Roscrea with a 13th-century castle, the pre-Palladian Damer House and walled gardens with a fountain.

ross-castle.expected_en: A 15th-century castle on the shores of Lough Leane, with boat trips.

rossmore-forest-park.expected_en: A former Rossmore estate with trails, wooden sculptures, lakes and the ruins of old gateways.

rothe-house-garden.expected_en: A 17th-century Tudor merchant's house, the only one of its kind open to the public in Ireland, with a historically recreated garden.

royal-canal-greenway.expected_en: A 130 km greenway along the Royal Canal, from Dublin to Cloondara — the final stretch is in Longford.

royal-hospital-kilmainham.expected_en: One of Dublin's most landmark buildings and Ireland's finest example of 17th-century architecture, today home to the Irish Museum of Modern Art.

russborough-house.expected_en: An 18th-century Palladian mansion with an ornate interior, a maze and views of the Wicklow Mountains.

sally-gap.expected_en: A scenic mountain pass in the Wicklow Mountains, surrounded by bogs where the rivers Liffey and Dargle rise.

saltee-islands.expected_en: A seabird sanctuary with one of Ireland's largest gannet colonies, reachable by boat from Kilmore Quay.

salthill.expected_en: Galway's seaside promenade, with a beach, a sea pool and views over the bay.

scattery-island.expected_en: A monastic island in the Shannon estuary, with a round tower, church ruins and a seal colony.

sean-mac-diarmada-cottage.expected_en: The birthplace of one of the signatories of the 1916 Proclamation, preserved as a museum in north Leitrim.

shannon-pot.expected_en: The source of the River Shannon, Ireland's longest river, in a karst pool on the slopes of Cuilcagh.

skellig-michael.expected_en: A UNESCO World Heritage Site: a 6th-century monastery atop a rocky island in the Atlantic, a Star Wars filming location.

sky-road.expected_en: A scenic coastal route around the Kingstown peninsula, with views of Clifden and the bay.

slane-castle.expected_en: A historic castle on the banks of the River Boyne, known for its concerts and distillery.

sliabh-beagh.expected_en: A bogland plateau on the border with Northern Ireland, with trails, a viewpoint and a visitor centre.

sliabh-liag.expected_en: Sea cliffs of almost 600 metres — among the highest in Europe — with the One Man's Pass trail.

slieve-bloom-mountains.expected_en: Mountains of bogland and forest between Laois and Offaly, with trails, waterfalls and panoramic viewpoints.

sligo-abbey.expected_en: A 13th-century Dominican abbey, the only one in Ireland with its original medieval high altar preserved.

smithwicks-experience.expected_en: A tour of Kilkenny's former brewery, where Smithwick's ale has been brewed since 1710.

sonairte-ecology-centre.expected_en: An ecology centre and organic garden on a historic farm near the sea, with trails and a vegetarian café.

spanish-arch-long-walk.expected_en: A 16th-century arch on the River Corrib and the colourful houses of the Long Walk, a Galway postcard view.

spanish-point-beach.expected_en: A sandy bay with calm waters and history linked to the Spanish Armada, popular with families and surfers.

spike-island-cork.expected_en: A fortress island in Cork harbour, once the world's largest prison, today an award-winning museum reached by ferry.

st-audens-church.expected_en: Dublin's only surviving medieval parish church, dedicated to the bishop of Rouen, with the St Anne's Guild Chapel and the Portlester tomb.

st-marys-abbey-chapter-house.expected_en: Remains of one of the largest and most important medieval monasteries in Ireland, accessible by guided tour only and open seasonally.

st-marys-cathedral-limerick.expected_en: A cathedral of 1168, Limerick's oldest building still in use, with rare medieval misericords.

st-marys-church-gowran.expected_en: A collegiate church from the late 13th century, with medieval Butler tombs and carvings by the "Gowran Master", now a national monument.

st-stephens-green.expected_en: One of Ireland's best-known public parks, in the heart of Dublin's shopping district, kept to its original Victorian layout.

strandhill-beach.expected_en: A surfing beach at the foot of Knocknarea, with surf schools, seaweed baths and a famous sunset.

strokestown-park-famine-museum.expected_en: A Georgian mansion with the National Famine Museum and restored walled gardens.

swiss-cottage.expected_en: An ornamental cottage of 1810, a perfect example of the "picturesque" style, with a restored interior and woodland.

the-main-guard.expected_en: A former 17th-century courthouse in the centre of Clonmel, with a restored sandstone columned arcade and an exhibition space.

the-model.expected_en: Sligo's art gallery and home of the Niland Collection, with important works by Jack B. Yeats and free admission to the galleries.

the-vee-bay-lough.expected_en: A V-shaped mountain pass with a viewpoint over the Suir valley and the glacial lake Bay Lough.

thoor-ballylee.expected_en: A 14th-century Norman tower where the poet W.B. Yeats lived, called by him "the most beautiful place on earth".

timahoe-round-tower.expected_en: A 12th-century round tower considered one of Ireland's most beautiful, with a richly decorated doorway.

tintern-abbey-wexford.expected_en: A Cistercian abbey founded in 1200 by William Marshal, with a Victorian colonnade and a wooded valley.

titanic-experience-cobh.expected_en: An interactive museum recreating the story of the Titanic and its link with Cobh.

torc-waterfall.expected_en: A 20-metre waterfall surrounded by woodland, on the slopes of Mount Torc.

trim-castle.expected_en: Ireland's largest Anglo-Norman castle, famous as a filming location for "Braveheart".

trinity-college-book-of-kells.expected_en: Ireland's iconic university and the famous Book of Kells, one of the most important medieval manuscripts in the world.

tullamore-dew-experience.expected_en: The Tullamore D.E.W. whiskey visitor centre in a 19th-century warehouse, with guided tastings.

valentia-island.expected_en: An island linked by bridge and ferry, with dinosaur footprints, subtropical gardens and the Cromwell Point lighthouse.

vandeleur-walled-garden.expected_en: A restored 19th-century walled garden, with a Victorian glasshouse and a café, in west Clare.

waterford-greenway.expected_en: A 46 km greenway along a former railway, with viaducts, a tunnel and a crossing of the River Suir — the most popular in Ireland.

waterford-treasures.expected_en: A group of museums about Viking and medieval Ireland, in the heart of the Viking Triangle.

westport-house.expected_en: A Georgian mansion of the Browne family with an adventure park, a small zoo and historic grounds.

wexford-wildfowl-reserve.expected_en: A nature reserve on the North Slob, winter home to one third of the world's Greenland white-fronted geese.

wicklow-historic-gaol.expected_en: An 18th-century prison turned interactive museum on two centuries of dark history.

wicklow-mountains-national-park.expected_en: A national park of mountains, lakes and glacial valleys — known as the "Garden of Ireland".

wicklow-way.expected_en: Ireland's oldest long-distance trail: 131 km through the Wicklow Mountains, from Dublin to Clonegal.

wild-nephin-ballycroy-national-park.expected_en: A national park of wild blanket bogs and the Nephin mountains, with a visitor centre and dark skies.

woodstock-gardens.expected_en: Restored Victorian gardens of the Tighe mansion, with an arboretum, an avenue of yews and views over the Nore valley.

apprenticeship-ie.expected_en: National portal to find apprenticeships in Ireland, combining on-the-job training with off-the-job training and opportunities across many occupational areas.

courses-ie.expected_en: Explore thousands of courses from colleges, universities, training providers and independent educators throughout Ireland.

etbi.expected_en: Find education and training opportunities offered through the network of Education and Training Boards in Ireland.

fetch-courses.expected_en: Find training and continuing education courses throughout Ireland, including apprenticeships, traineeships, PLC courses, adult education and other FET opportunities.

local-enterprise-office.expected_en: Training programmes and business courses for those starting, developing or growing a business in Ireland.

microcreds.expected_en: Explore short, flexible micro-credentials awarded by Irish universities, with options in areas such as business, technology, education, health and other professional fields.

qualifax.expected_en: Ireland's national database for courses and student guidance, helping students, jobseekers and adults explore education and training options.

skillnet-ireland.expected_en: Discover training and reskilling opportunities designed around the needs of companies, employees and industry sectors throughout Ireland.

solas-ecollege.expected_en: SOLAS online learning and skills development, including digital skills, IT, project management, business and other areas.

springboard-plus.expected_en: Discover subsidised further education courses designed to help people requalify, build skills and develop new career opportunities.
